questions.question: Who wrote the three-volume history of Akbar's reign?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Abul Fazl**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Abul Fazl** was a prominent courtier, historian, and writer in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar. • He authored the **three-volume history** of Akbar's reign titled **Akbarnama**, which is one of the most celebrated chronicles of the Mughal era. • The **Akbarnama** is divided into three parts: the first part deals with Akbar's ancestors, the second part focuses on Akbar's reign, and the third part is the **Ain-i-Akbari**, a detailed account of the administration and culture of the empire. • Abul Fazl's work is considered an **authentic and detailed source** of Mughal history and administration during Akbar's reign. • He was also known for his literary style and contributions to Persian literature. He played a significant role in shaping Akbar's policies and was one of the **Nine Gems (Navratnas)** of Akbar's court.

questions.question:
Which of the following pair of dynasty - region is correct?

I. Rashtrakuta - Tamil Nadu

Il. Gurjara-Pratihara - Rajasthan
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Statement I: Rashtrakuta - Tamil Nadu** 

• The **Rashtrakutas** were a prominent dynasty in Indian history, ruling from the 8th to 10th century CE.

• They primarily ruled over the Deccan region, with their empire extending across parts of modern-day **Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh**.

• They did not have Tamil Nadu as a significant part of their empire. Hence, *this statement is incorrect.*

• **Statement II: Gurjara-Pratihara - Rajasthan** 

• The **Gurjara-Pratiharas** were a powerful dynasty in northern India, especially during the 8th to 11th centuries.

• They had a stronghold in parts of modern-day **Rajasthan**, along with regions of Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh.

• Their capital was initially at **Bhinmal (Rajasthan)**, later shifting to Kanauj, which became a prominent center of their empire. Hence, *this statement is correct.*

• Based on the above, only **Statement II** is correct, making the correct option **Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__

• **Rashtrakutas**: 

• The Rashtrakutas were known for their contributions to art and architecture, notably the **Kailasa Temple at Ellora**, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

• They ruled from their capital at **Manyakheta** (modern-day Malkhed in Karnataka).

• Their empire was known for its tolerance towards different religions, including **Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism**.

• The Rashtrakutas played a significant role in southern India but did not have Tamil Nadu as a major part of their territory.

• **Gurjara-Pratiharas**: 

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas were one of the three major dynasties involved in the tripartite struggle for control over **Kanauj**, alongside the Rashtrakutas and the Palas.

• Their capital, Kanauj, became a prominent political and cultural hub during their reign.

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas are also known for their patronage of art and architecture, including the construction of temples in **Rajasthan** and other regions.

• They played a crucial role in defending India against Arab invasions in the early medieval period.

• **Key Characteristics of Tamil Nadu During the Rashtrakuta Period**: 

• Tamil Nadu during this period was dominated by the **Pallavas** and later the **Cholas**.

• These dynasties were responsible for some of the iconic Dravidian architecture, including the temples at Mahabalipuram and Thanjavur.

• The Rashtrakutas had limited influence in Tamil Nadu, focusing more on the Deccan and central India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Rashtrakutas:** Their empire was at its peak under **Amoghavarsha I**, who was known for his contributions to Kannada literature.

• **Gurjara-Pratiharas:** The dynasty declined after the invasions of the **Turks** and internal conflicts.

• **Tripartite Struggle:** This was a prolonged conflict between the **Rashtrakutas, Gurjara-Pratiharas, and Palas** for control over northern India.

• **Tamil Nadu:** Dominated by the Chola dynasty during the medieval period, which was known for its maritime power and contributions to art and architecture.

questions.question: Article 40 of the Indian constitution is related with ___________

options.text: Free medical aid to the citizen

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Organization of village panchayats**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• **Article 40** of the **Indian Constitution** is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which are guidelines for the state to frame laws and policies aimed at establishing social and economic democracy. 
• It directs the state to take measures to **organize village panchayats** and endow them with such powers and authority to function as units of **self-government**. 
• The goal of Article 40 is to promote grassroots democracy through the establishment of **local self-governance** systems across villages in India. 
• The implementation of Article 40 led to the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). 
• Under this amendment, a three-tier Panchayati Raj system was introduced, consisting of **Gram Panchayats, Panchayat Samiti,** and **Zila Parishad**, enabling decentralized governance and local decision-making. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:** 
• These principles are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution of India and aim to create a just and equitable society. 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, but serve as important guidelines for governance. 
• Examples of DPSPs include promoting education, protecting the environment, and establishing village panchayats. 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:** 
• This amendment added **Part IX** to the Constitution and provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). 
• It mandated the establishment of a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj in villages, intermediate levels, and districts. 
• It introduced provisions for **regular elections**, reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and women, and the creation of State Election Commissions. 
• **Functions of Panchayati Raj Institutions:** 
• PRIs play a crucial role in **rural development** by implementing schemes related to health, education, sanitation, and agriculture. 
• They also enable participatory governance, where citizens can directly engage in decision-making processes. 
• **Related Articles in the Constitution:** 
• **Article 243**: Defines the Panchayati Raj system and its structure. 
• **Article 243D**: Provides for reservation in PRIs for SCs, STs, and women. 
• **Article 243E**: Specifies the duration and terms of office for members of Panchayati Raj Institutions. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Context:** 
• India has a long tradition of local self-governance, with village panchayats mentioned in ancient texts like the **Manusmriti** and **Kautilya's Arthashastra**. 
• The concept of Panchayati Raj was revived during India's freedom movement, particularly by leaders like **Mahatma Gandhi**, who emphasized village self-reliance. 
• **Challenges in Implementation:** 
• Despite constitutional provisions, Panchayati Raj Institutions often face issues like inadequate funding, limited autonomy, and interference by higher authorities. 
• Capacity building and training programs for elected representatives are essential to improve the functioning of PRIs. </ul

questions.question: Provisions of the Sixth Schedule of the Indian constitution does not apply to which of these states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Sixth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution was specifically designed to provide **autonomy to tribal areas** in certain northeastern states of India.
 
• It applies to the **tribal areas** of **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**.
 
• The provisions under the Sixth Schedule allow for the creation of **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)**, which have legislative, judicial, and executive powers in certain specified areas.
 
• **Manipur** is not covered under the Sixth Schedule. Instead, it has its own distinct arrangements for the governance of tribal areas, such as the Hill Areas Committee and Autonomous District Councils (not under the Sixth Schedule).
 
• The absence of Sixth Schedule provisions in Manipur is due to its unique historical and administrative context, where different mechanisms are in place for tribal development and administration.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Manipur.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sixth Schedule and Autonomous District Councils (ADCs):**

 
 
• The Sixth Schedule provides for the administration of tribal areas through **Autonomous District Councils** (ADCs), which have the authority to make laws on certain matters such as land, forest management, village administration, and inheritance of property.
 
• Each ADC consists of not more than 30 members, of whom four are nominated by the governor, while the rest are elected members.
 
• ADCs have the power to create courts for trial of certain cases and also manage resources within their jurisdiction.
 
• Examples of ADCs include the **Bodoland Territorial Council** in Assam and the **Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council** in Meghalaya.
 
 
 
• **States Covered under the Sixth Schedule:**
 
 
• The states covered under the Sixth Schedule include **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**.
 
• This schedule was incorporated to protect the rights and culture of tribal communities in these states.
 
 
 
• **Manipur and Tribal Governance:**
 
 
• Manipur has **Autonomous District Councils** created under the **Manipur (Hill Areas) District Councils Act, 1971**, but these councils do not have the same constitutional protection as those under the Sixth Schedule.
 
• The **Hill Areas Committee**, constituted under Article 371C of the Indian Constitution, is responsible for protecting the interests of tribal communities in Manipur.
 
 
 
• **Differences in Governance:**
 
 
• While the Sixth Schedule grants legislative and judicial powers to ADCs, the ADCs in Manipur operate under state legislation and have limited powers compared to their counterparts in Sixth Schedule areas.
 
• This distinction highlights the unique governance framework adopted in Manipur to address its tribal population's needs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 244:**

 
 
• This article of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of Scheduled and Tribal Areas.
 
• It provides for the application of the **Fifth Schedule** in other states (excluding northeastern states) and the **Sixth Schedule** in northeastern states.
 
 
 
• **Role of Governor:**
 
 
• The governor plays a significant role in the administration of Sixth Schedule areas and has the power to create or dissolve ADCs and regulate their functioning.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Sixth Schedule was introduced in the Constitution to address the aspirations of tribal communities in the northeastern region, ensuring their autonomy and preserving their unique identity.

questions.question: Who assumed the Chief Ministership of Odisha in June 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohan Charan Majhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Mohan Charan Majhi** assumed the position of the **Chief Minister of Odisha** in **June 2024**.

• He succeeded **Naveen Patnaik**, who served as the Chief Minister of Odisha for a record-breaking tenure starting from **2000**.

• **Mohan Charan Majhi** is a leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**. His appointment marks a significant shift in the state's political dynamics.

• His leadership focuses on issues such as **development, employment generation, and addressing regional disparities** in Odisha.

• The change in leadership is part of the **2024 Odisha State Assembly elections**, where BJP emerged with a strong mandate, ending the long-standing rule of the Biju Janata Dal (BJD).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Naveen Patnaik:** 

• **Naveen Patnaik** served as the Chief Minister of Odisha for over two decades, leading the **Biju Janata Dal (BJD)** to multiple electoral victories.

• His tenure was marked by significant progress in areas such as **infrastructure development, disaster management, and healthcare.**

• He implemented schemes like **KALIA (Krushak Assistance for Livelihood and Income Augmentation)** to support farmers.

• **Mohan Charan Majhi:** 

• **Mohan Charan Majhi** hails from Odisha and has been an active political figure representing the **BJP**.

• He has emphasized the importance of **improving education, healthcare, and industrialization** in Odisha.

• His party’s victory in the 2024 elections was driven by promises of **inclusive governance and development-focused policies.**

• **Odisha Politics in 2024:** 

• The 2024 elections saw a significant political shift as the BJP gained prominence, ending the dominance of the **BJD.**

• Key issues included unemployment, regional development, and better disaster preparedness.

• The BJP's campaign focused on connecting with grassroots voters and leveraging national-level support.

• **Important State-Level Initiatives:** 

• **KALIA Scheme:** Aimed at providing financial assistance to small and marginal farmers in Odisha.

• **Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana:** Focused on providing universal health coverage to the people of Odisha.

• **Mission Shakti:** Empowering women through self-help groups and entrepreneurship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **BJP's Emergence:** 

• The BJP's strong performance in the 2024 Odisha elections marked a significant political transition in the state.

• The party focused on regional development and connecting with marginalized communities.

• **Challenges for the New Leadership:** 

• Mohan Charan Majhi faces the challenge of maintaining political stability and addressing socio-economic disparities in Odisha.

• Disaster management remains a critical focus area for the new government.

• Industrial growth and job creation will be key priorities under his leadership.

questions.question: In April 2025, the Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi approved the Vibrant Villages Programme - II (WP - ll) as a ______ percent centre funded scheme.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100 percent**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Vibrant Villages Programme - II (VVP-II)** was approved by the **Union Cabinet** chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** in **April 2025**. 
• It is a **100 percent centrally funded scheme**, which means the central government will bear the entire cost of the program. This eliminates any financial burden on state governments. 
• The main objective of the **Vibrant Villages Programme - II** is to **develop and strengthen border villages** in strategically important areas, ensuring better infrastructure, connectivity, and socio-economic development. 
• The program aims to counter **border challenges** by focusing on **village development in remote and isolated areas**, ensuring improved standards of living for people residing there. 
• The scheme involves **multi-sectoral projects** such as **road connectivity, housing, livelihood generation, and basic amenities** to ensure holistic development. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Vibrant Villages Programme Background:** 
• The **Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP)** was first launched to address the challenges faced by people living in **India's border villages**, particularly in areas near the **China border** in states like **Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh, Uttarakhand, and Sikkim**. 
• The program focuses on **community development** and reducing out-migration by providing better opportunities and facilities in border areas. 
• **VVP-II** is an extension of the original program, with increased funding and a broader scope to cover more villages. 
• **100 Percent Centrally Funded Scheme:** 
• A 100% centrally funded scheme implies that the **entire financial allocation** is provided by the **Government of India**, ensuring **uniform implementation** across the targeted areas. 
• Such schemes are typically designed for **strategically important regions** or areas requiring **special attention**, such as border regions. 
• **Strategic Importance of Border Villages:** 
• Border villages are often **isolated and underdeveloped**, making them vulnerable to **external influences** and challenges related to **national security**. 
• The development of these villages is critical to ensuring **territorial integrity** and fostering a sense of belonging among residents. 
• **Key Features of VVP-II:** 
• **Infrastructure Development**: Construction of roads, bridges, schools, and healthcare facilities in border villages. 
• **Livelihood Opportunities**: Promoting skill development, local industries, and tourism to create employment. 
• **Connectivity**: Enhancing digital and physical connectivity to integrate border areas with the rest of the country. 
• **Social Development**: Providing access to education, healthcare, and basic amenities like water and sanitation. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Funding Structure:** 
• Unlike schemes with shared funding (e.g., **60:40 ratio** between Centre and States), **100% funding** means complete financial support from the Centre, ensuring faster implementation. 
• **Similar Programs:** 
• **Border Area Development Programme (BADP):** Aimed at improving border infrastructure to enhance security and support local communities. 
• **PM Gati Shakti:** Focused on improving connectivity and infrastructure across India, including remote areas. 
• **National Security Implications:** 
• Developing border villages strengthens **India's defense capabilities** by creating **self-reliant communities** in remote regions. 
• It also addresses **migration issues** by providing better opportunities for residents, reducing population decline in critical areas. </ul

questions.question: Technology and innovation report is published by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UNCTAD**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Technology and Innovation Report** is published by the **United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)**. 
• **UNCTAD** is a permanent intergovernmental body established by the **United Nations General Assembly in 1964**. 
• The **Technology and Innovation Report** examines the role of science, technology, and innovation in driving sustainable development and reducing inequality across the globe. 
• UNCTAD focuses on how **technological advancements** can be leveraged by developing countries to bridge the socio-economic gaps with developed nations. 
• The report provides **policy recommendations** to address challenges related to technology transfer, digital divide, and sustainable innovation. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **About UNCTAD:** 
• UNCTAD stands for **United Nations Conference on Trade and Development**. 
• It is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**. 
• The main objective of UNCTAD is to promote **inclusive and sustainable economic development**, especially in developing nations. 
• It works on areas such as trade policy, investment, technology, and financing for development. 
• **Key Features of the Technology and Innovation Report:** 
• The report identifies **emerging technologies** like artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, nanotechnology, and biotechnology that have the potential to transform industries. 
• It emphasizes the importance of **bridging the digital divide** between developing and developed countries. 
• The report examines **policy measures** that countries can adopt to align technological advancements with sustainable development goals (SDGs). 
• **Other Reports Published by UNCTAD:** 
• **Trade and Development Report:** Focuses on global economic trends and development policies. 
• **World Investment Report:** Analyzes global foreign direct investment (FDI) trends and policies. 
• **Economic Development in Africa Report:** Explores key development challenges and opportunities for African nations. 
• **UNCTAD’s Role in Technology Development:** 
• UNCTAD assists developing countries in adopting **digital technologies** to enhance trade and economic growth. 
• It supports nations in formulating **national innovation policies** and promoting technology transfer. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **UNCTAD Membership:** 
• UNCTAD has **195 member states**, including all members of the United Nations and the Holy See. 
• It operates as a forum for governments to discuss policy issues related to trade, investment, and development. 
• **Relation to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** 
• UNCTAD supports the achievement of **SDG 9** (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) by promoting technological advancements. 
• It also contributes to **SDG 8** (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and **SDG 17** (Partnerships for the Goals). 
• **Global Impact:** 
• UNCTAD’s reports and recommendations have influenced **global trade policies** and development strategies. 
• Its focus on technology ensures that developing countries are not left behind in the **Fourth Industrial Revolution**.

questions.question: International Solar Alliance (ISA) aims to mobilize _______ trillion dollar in solar investments by 2030.

• ISA has set a target to mobilize **1 trillion dollars** in solar investments by **2030** to support the development of solar energy infrastructure, technology innovation, and capacity building. 
• The alliance focuses on countries that lie between the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, as these regions receive abundant sunlight throughout the year, enabling large-scale solar energy generation. 
• ISA works to promote cooperation among its member countries, share knowledge and technology, and pool financial resources to achieve its ambitious goals. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __

• It aims to bring together countries to work collaboratively on **solar technologies**, **solar financing**, and **capacity building**. 
• ISA has **112 member countries** as of 2023, primarily from regions with high solar potential. 
• It facilitates the development of solar projects by offering technical assistance, capacity building, and financial support. 
• India hosts the headquarters of ISA, located in **Gurugram, Haryana**. This highlights India's leadership role in promoting solar energy. 
• ISA initiatives include programs like **Affordable Finance at Scale** and **Scaling Solar Applications for Agriculture Use** to maximize solar energy deployment.

• The global solar energy market is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of **20%** from 2023 to 2030. 
• Major solar energy projects include India's **Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park**, China's **Tengger Desert Solar Park**, and the US's **Ivanpah Solar Power Facility**. 
• Innovative technologies like **solar panels**, **solar thermal systems**, and **solar batteries** are driving the adoption of solar energy worldwide.

questions.question: Which two countries are collaborating on the ‘TRISHNA' mission launched in June 2024?

• The mission is being jointly developed by **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and the **French space agency CNES (Centre National d'Études Spatiales)**.

• TRISHNA aims to provide high-resolution thermal infrared data for applications like **climate monitoring, water resource management, and agricultural practices**.

• The satellite will help in monitoring **land surface temperatures** and other critical parameters to address global challenges such as **climate change** and **water scarcity**.

• The mission is scheduled to launch in **June 2024**, showcasing the ongoing international collaboration in space exploration between India and France.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• India and France have a longstanding partnership in the field of space exploration, dating back to the **1960s**.

• Prominent collaborations include the **MEGHA-TROPIQUES** mission for studying tropical weather and the **SARAL (Satellite with ARgos and ALtiKa)** mission for oceanographic studies.

• Both countries are committed to advancing research in areas like **climate change, Earth observation, and interplanetary exploration**.

• **Applications of TRISHNA Mission:**

• The satellite will provide data on **land surface temperature** with high spatial and temporal resolution, aiding in **agricultural monitoring**, including water stress and crop health.

• It will support studies on **urban heat islands** and their impact on climate change.

• The data can also help in **disaster management** by monitoring heatwaves, droughts, and forest fires.

• **ISRO's Role:**

• The space agency has extensive experience in Earth observation missions, including successful launches like the **Cartosat** and **Resourcesat series**.

• **CNES's Contribution:**

• CNES will provide the thermal infrared instrument for TRISHNA.

• The French space agency has expertise in developing advanced instruments for Earth observation and climate studies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **TRISHNA's Unique Features:**

• The satellite will provide **high spatial and temporal resolution data**, which will be critical for addressing challenges related to environmental monitoring.

• It will complement existing missions like NASA's **ECOSTRESS**, enhancing global understanding of Earth's thermal processes.

• **Global Importance of Thermal Imaging Satellites:**

• Thermal imaging helps in understanding the impact of human activities on natural resources and climate.

• Such satellites play a key role in monitoring **water usage, irrigation efficiency, and forest conservation**.

• **India's Growing Role in Space Exploration:**

• India has emerged as a leader in cost-effective satellite launches and space missions.

• Missions like **Mangalyaan**, **Chandrayaan**, and **PSLV launches** have established ISRO as a major player in space technology.

questions.question:
Who was in the combined forces that attacked Tipu Sultan in 1792?

I. The Marathas

ll. The Nizam of Hyderabad

III. The East India Company
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II, and III**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• In **1792**, Tipu Sultan faced a combined military assault during the Third Anglo-Mysore War. 
• The forces that attacked Tipu Sultan consisted of three major powers: **The Marathas**, **The Nizam of Hyderabad**, and **The East India Company**. 
• Tipu Sultan was forced to sign the **Treaty of Seringapatam** (1792), where he lost a significant portion of his territory to these combined forces. *Hence, statement I, II, and III are correct.* 
• The East India Company led the campaign under **Lord Cornwallis**, who was the Governor-General of India during the time. 
• This coalition was formed to counter Tipu Sultan's growing influence and his alliance with the French, which was seen as a threat by the British and other Indian rulers. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Tipu Sultan:** 
• Tipu Sultan, also known as the **Tiger of Mysore**, was the ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore and a prominent figure in Indian history. 
• He was known for his military prowess, administrative reforms, and resistance against British colonial forces. 
• Tipu Sultan introduced new military tactics and modernized his army with the help of French advisors. 
• He was one of the few Indian rulers who actively sought alliances with foreign powers, especially **France**, to counter British imperialism. 
• **The Marathas:** 
• The Marathas were a powerful confederacy in India during the 18th century and controlled vast territories across the subcontinent. 
• They joined the coalition against Tipu Sultan, fearing his growing dominance in the region. 
• The Marathas played a crucial role in the Third Anglo-Mysore War, contributing troops and resources to the allied forces. 
• **The Nizam of Hyderabad:** 
• The Nizam of Hyderabad allied with the British and the Marathas against Tipu Sultan. 
• This alliance was strategic, as the Nizam sought to maintain his own position in the Deccan region. 
• The Nizam provided military assistance to the coalition forces, which ultimately led to Tipu Sultan's defeat. 
• **The East India Company:** 
• The East India Company, under **Lord Cornwallis**, played a leading role in the Third Anglo-Mysore War. 
• The Company's primary goal was to curb Tipu Sultan's power and secure its own trade interests in southern India. 
• After Tipu Sultan's defeat, the Company gained significant territorial advantages through the Treaty of Seringapatam. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Treaty of Seringapatam (1792):** 
• As a result of the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Tipu Sultan signed the Treaty of Seringapatam. 
• He had to cede half of his kingdom to the allied forces, including the British, Marathas, and Nizam. 
• Tipu also agreed to pay a substantial war indemnity and surrender two of his sons as hostages. 
• **Impact of the Coalition:** 
• The coalition weakened Tipu Sultan's position and marked a significant step in British dominance over southern India. 
• It showcased the strategic alliances formed by the East India Company with Indian rulers to expand its influence. 
• The war highlighted the importance of diplomacy and alliances in shaping India's colonial history. </ul

questions.question: Which of the following can recommend the creation of a Legislative Council in an Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Legislative Assembly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The power to recommend the creation of a **Legislative Council** in a state lies with the **State Legislative Assembly**. This is done through the passing of a resolution by the assembly in favor of such a creation.
 
• According to **Article 169** of the Indian Constitution, the **State Legislative Assembly** must pass the resolution with a majority of its total membership and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
 
• Once the resolution is passed, the Parliament is empowered to create or abolish the Legislative Council in the state by enacting a law.
 
• The role of the **Governor**, **President**, or **Chief Minister** is not directly involved in the initiation or recommendation process for the creation of the Legislative Council.</

questions.question: What is the transport of soluble products of photosynthesis in a plant known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Translocation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Translocation** refers to the movement of soluble products of photosynthesis, such as sugars, from leaves (source) to other parts of the plant (sink).
 
• This process occurs in the **phloem tissue**, which is specialized for transporting organic nutrients.
 
• The products of photosynthesis are transported in the form of **sucrose** to growing regions, storage organs, seeds, or roots.
 
• Translocation is an active process requiring **energy** in the form of ATP, as it often involves movement against a concentration gradient.
 
• The pressure-flow hypothesis explains translocation: sugars are actively loaded into the phloem, creating a high osmotic pressure that drives the flow towards the sink regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transpiration:**

 
 
• Transpiration is the process by which water evaporates from the surface of leaves, primarily through the **stomata**.
 
• It helps in the uptake of minerals and cooling of the plant but is **not related to the transport of photosynthetic products**.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation:**
 
 
• Evaporation refers to the phase change of water from liquid to vapor, occurring on surfaces exposed to air.
 
• This is a physical process and does not involve the transport of nutrients or sugars.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion:**
 
 
• Diffusion is the passive movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration.
 
• While diffusion occurs in plants, it is **not the primary mechanism** for long-distance transport of photosynthetic products.
 
 
 
• **Phloem Tissue:**
 
 
• Phloem consists of specialized cells such as **sieve tube elements** and companion cells, which facilitate the transport of organic nutrients.
 
• The companion cells play a vital role in loading and unloading sugars into sieve tubes.
 
 
 
• **Pressure-Flow Hypothesis:**
 
 
• This widely accepted model explains the movement of sugars in plants through the phloem.
 
• It describes how osmotic pressure gradients drive the movement of nutrients from source (high sugar concentration) to sink (low sugar concentration).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of ATP in Translocation:** ATP is required for the active loading of sucrose into the phloem, particularly in source regions like leaves.
 
• **Source and Sink:** The source refers to the regions where sugars are produced (e.g., leaves), while the sink refers to areas requiring sugars for growth or storage (e.g., roots, fruits).
 
• **Phloem Loading:** Companion cells use active transport mechanisms to load sucrose into sieve tubes, creating a pressure gradient.
 
• **Bidirectional Transport:** Unlike xylem (unidirectional transport of water), translocation in phloem can occur in multiple directions based on the plant's needs.
 
• **Significance:** Translocation ensures the distribution of energy-rich compounds, enabling growth, development, and reproduction in plants.

questions.question: The ‘Tattvarthadhigamasutra’, regarded as the first book on Jaina philosophy, was authored by _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Umasvati**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **The 'Tattvarthadhigamasutra'** is regarded as the first authoritative text on **Jaina philosophy**. It is considered a foundational scripture for both the **Svetambara** and **Digambara** sects of Jainism. 
• The text was authored by **Umasvati**, also known as **Umasvami**, a renowned Jain scholar. He lived around the 2nd to 3rd century CE, making this text a pivotal work of Jain literature. 
• The Tattvarthadhigamasutra is written in **Sanskrit** and is structured as an aphoristic text, making it concise yet comprehensive in elucidating Jain philosophy and doctrine. 
• The book systematically explains the **seven fundamental truths (Tattvas)** in Jainism, including concepts like right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct, which are critical for liberation (Moksha). 
• It is one of the few Jain texts written in Sanskrit, as most Jain scriptures are traditionally in **Prakrit**. Its use of Sanskrit allowed it to reach a broader intellectual audience in ancient India. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Umasvati and His Contributions:** 
• Umasvati is considered a unifying figure in Jainism, as his work is respected by both major sects of Jainism: **Svetambara** and **Digambara**. 
• He is believed to have been born in the Kushan Empire era and is credited with making Jain philosophy accessible to a scholarly audience. 
• **Content of the Tattvarthadhigamasutra:** 
• The text is divided into **10 chapters**, dealing with topics such as the nature of reality, the soul, karma, and liberation. 
• It outlines the path of **three jewels** (Ratnatraya) in Jainism: **Samyak Darshana (Right Faith), Samyak Jnana (Right Knowledge),** and **Samyak Charitra (Right Conduct)**. 
• **Importance of the Tattvarthadhigamasutra:** 
• It serves as a bridge between Jain philosophy and mainstream Indian philosophical thought, engaging with concepts like the **nature of the soul and metaphysics**. 
• The text has been extensively commented on by later Jain scholars, which further expanded its influence and interpretation. 
• **Other Options Explained:** 
• **Mahavira:** Mahavira is the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism and is credited with organizing Jain teachings into a structured form but did not author the Tattvarthadhigamasutra. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.*** 
• **Bhadrabahu:** Bhadrabahu was a Jain monk and scholar, known for his role in preserving Jain texts and traditions, but he was not the author of this text. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.*** 
• **Rishabhadeva:** Rishabhadeva, or Lord Rishabha, is the first Tirthankara of Jainism, revered for introducing the concept of asceticism, but he is not associated with the Tattvarthadhigamasutra. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Jain Philosophy:** Jainism emphasizes the principles of **Ahimsa (non-violence), Aparigraha (non-possessiveness),** and **Satya (truthfulness)**, forming the ethical core of the religion. 
• **Karma in Jainism:** Jainism presents a unique perspective on karma, viewing it as a material substance that binds to the soul due to actions, and liberation is achieved by shedding this karma. 
• **Role of Tirthankaras:** The Tirthankaras are spiritual teachers who achieve liberation and help guide others on the path to Moksha. Mahavira is the most prominent among them. 
• **Canonical Texts:** Jain scriptures are divided into two categories: **Agamas** (canonical texts) and **Non-Agamas** (commentaries and other works). The Tattvarthadhigamasutra falls into the latter category. </ul
